title: A photographic identification key for the embryonic development of Crangon crangon Linnaeus 1758 (Decapoda: Caridea) and practical guidelines for egg preservation
content:
Abstract
The common brown shrimp (Crangon crangon Linnaeus 1758) is among the predominant crustacean species in the Wadden Sea, playing a crucial role in the food web and supporting a widespread commercial fishery. Despite being essential for recruitment and life cycle understanding, egg development in C. crangon has so far been described only in textual form, and only very few studies worked, or reported on suitable preservation methods of egg bearing females or eggs. Based on laboratory-reared eggs, we developed a visual identification key using digital imaging that facilitates consistent staging of embryos across studies and regions, and provides a practical tool for technicians, students, and fisheries managers using routine stereomicroscopy. We also investigated the effects of four different preservation protocols, namely, cooking + freezing, freezing only, 70% ethanol, and 4% formalin emersion, on the appearance and the size of the eggs of C. crangon. We found freezing only to be the preservation methods yielding the best results.
